trinkets.description_en: Using an active item triggers the effect of an additional 1-2 charge active item
trinkets.description_zh: 使用主动道具时, 额外触发随机1-2充能的主动道具
trinkets.wiki_description: Once per room, using an active item triggers another random active item effect.

trinkets.name: Beth's Essence
trinkets.description_en:
Entering an Angel Room spawns 5 wisps
Donating to Beggars has a 25% chance to spawn a wisp
trinkets.description_zh:
进入天使房时, 生成5魂火
向乞丐捐钱时, 25%概率生成1魂火
trinkets.wiki_description: Upon entering an Angel Room, spawns 5 wisp orbitals. Giving money to Beggars can spawn wisps.

trinkets.name: The Twins
trinkets.description_en:
50% chance to duplicate a familiar each room
Grants Brother Bobby or Sister Maggy if Isaac has no familiars
trinkets.description_zh:
每个房间有50%概率复制1个跟班
若角色没有跟班, 则获得波比兄弟或玛姬姐妹
trinkets.wiki_description: Adds a chance to duplicate one of Isaac's familiars when entering a new room.

trinkets.name: Adoption Papers
trinkets.description_en: Shops sell familiars for 10 coins
trinkets.description_zh: 商店的道具由跟班取代, 售价10硬币
trinkets.wiki_description: Shops can sell familiars, which will always be at a discounted price.

trinkets.name: Cricket Leg
trinkets.description_en: Killing an enemy has a 17% chance to spawn a random locust
trinkets.description_zh: 杀死敌人时, 17%概率生成1只随机蝗虫
trinkets.wiki_description: Adds a 1/6 chance to spawn a random locust when killing an enemy.

trinkets.name: Apollyon's Best Friend
trinkets.description_en: Grants 1 Abyss locust
trinkets.description_zh: 生成1只无底坑蝗虫
trinkets.wiki_description: Spawns an Abyss locust familiar which will fly forward while Isaac shoots.

trinkets.name: Broken Glasses
trinkets.description_en:
50% chance of adding an extra blind item in Treasure Rooms
50% chance to reveal the blind item in alt path Treasure Rooms
trinkets.description_zh:
50%概率在宝箱房添加1个额外的问号道具
 50%概率揭示替代章节的问号道具
trinkets.wiki_description: Gives a 50% chance to add a '?' item to Treasure Rooms. Only one item can be taken. The extra items on the alt path are revealed instead.

trinkets.name: Ice Cube
trinkets.description_en:
Entering a room has a 20% chance to petrify random enemies
 Killing a petrified enemy freezes it
trinkets.description_zh:
进入房间时, 20%概率石化1个敌人
 击杀石化的敌人可将其冻结
trinkets.wiki_description: Adds a chance to petrify enemies when entering the room. Killing the petrified enemy freezes it.

trinkets.name: Sigil of Baphomet
trinkets.description_en:
Killing an enemy makes Isaac invincible for 1 second
Invincibility stacks with successive enemy kills, up to 5 seconds
trinkets.description_zh:
击杀敌人时, 使角色获得1秒护盾
期间击杀敌人可以累加, 最多5秒
trinkets.wiki_description: Grants an invulnerability shield for 1 second after killing an enemy.

cards.name: 0 - The Fool
cards.description_en: Teleports Isaac to the first room of the floor
cards.description_zh: 将角色传送至本层初始房间

cards.name: I - The Magician
cards.quote: May you never miss your goal
cards.description_en:
Receive for the room:

room_guides.Achievements:
{{Hatnote|For tips and strategies on completing achievements, see [[achievement tip]]s.}}

'''Achievements''' are unlocked after completing [[Challenge]]s, reaching certain [[completion mark|milestones]], achieving hidden goals, or unlocking certain [[item]]s. In the PC version, every Steam achievement exactly corresponds to one secret in-game, whereas only a handful of secrets are represented by PSN trophies in the PlayStation version of the game.

If Isaac is unable to unlock achievements, a small icon of a crossed-out trophy {{no unlocks}} will be displayed below the {{e|Key}}'s counter. Conditions which can disable the ability to unlock achievements include:
* Using a pre-determined [[seed]]. {{dlc|a}} Certain cosmetic and difficulty-increasing [[seed|special seeds]] will still allow unlocks.
* During a [[Challenge]], although the achievement for completing the challenge is unaffected.
* {{dlc|a}} During a [[Daily Challenge]], although the achievements associated with this game mode are unaffected.
* {{dlc|a+}} Playing with any enabled [[mod]] (unless {{e|Mom}} has been beaten).
* {{dlc|a+}} During [[Victory Lap]]s.
* {{dlc|r}} If the [[Debug Console]] is enabled (unless {{e|Mom}} has been beaten).
* {{dlc|r+}} Joining an in progress [[Online (open beta)|Online]] run.

Rebirth has a total of 178 unlockable secrets. {{dlc|a}} [[Afterbirth]] added 98 new secrets, for a total of 276. {{dlc|a+}} [[Afterbirth †]] added 63 new secrets, for a total of 339. {{dlc|a+}} [[Booster Pack #5]] added 64 new secrets, for a total of 403. {{dlc|r}} [[Repentance]] added 234 new secrets, for a total of 637.
{{dlc|r+}} [[Repentance+]] added 4 new secrets, for a total of 641.

Inside the stats menu, while having the "secrets" menu open, pressing Alt + F2 will sync unlocks with Steam achievements. If you have Steam achievements for secrets that haven't been unlocked in-game, they will be unlocked by doing this.

== Notes ==
* {{dlc+|r}} The {{a|5 Nights at Mom's}} achievement is bugged in various ways:
** {{dlc|nr+}} {{plat|PC}} Because the game uses 32-bit architecture and has [[Custom Challenges#Characters (playertype)|41]] characters, the game counts wins twice for the first 9 characters. That means if in your streak you play once with a character from Isaac to Lazarus, you will get the achievement with 4 wins. If you play with two characters from Isaac to Lazarus, you will get the achievement with 3 wins. Since the game uses 64-bit architecture on consoles, this bug is PC-only.
** Using normal [[Characters]] to get a win and then using its tainted counterpart won't work, only one of them will work for obtaining the achievement.
*** Additionally, due to integer overflow, some tainted characters share the same bitmask with some normal characters. The game resets the achievement streak counter if two runs are done with characters with the same bitmask. {{c|Tainted Lilith}} has the same bitmask as {{c|Isaac}}. Here are the pairs of characters that have the same bitmask : Tainted Keeper and Magdalene, Tainted Apollyon and Cain, Tainted Forgotten and Lazarus, Tainted Bethany and ???, Tainted Jacob and Eve, Tainted Dead Lazarus and Samson, Tainted Jacob in Lost form and Azazel. If you did a run with Isaac or Lilith, do not finish a run with Tainted Lilith or the counter will reset. Not confirmed yet but by the same logic as the bug above, this one is likely PC-only too.
** The achievement does not unlock in Co-op Repentance, even if the five wins were done with different characters for each player.
** Modded characters do not interfere with the streaks, and do not reset nor increment the counter.{{dlc-}}

room_guides.Angel Room:
Angel Rooms are the divine equivalent of the Devil Room. They feature an angel and 0-4 free items. Taking one of these items causes all other free items to disappear. (Tainted Keeper still needs to pay for these items, and buying any of them causes all of the others to disappear. Some of these items cost 30 pennies to buy.)
Every time the Devil Room is spawned/entered, there's a chance for it to be replaced by the Angel Room if certain conditions are met. After beating the Dark Room or Chest once, an Angel can be awoken by planting a bomb near the statue (or destroying it with Leo or similar items). This will begin an angel boss fight and allow Isaac to charge his active item and pick up Key Piece 1 or Key Piece 2. Both pieces are needed to get through the Golden Door in Chest or Dark Room to fight Mega Satan.


== Layouts ==

=== Angel Shops ===
Angel shops are special angel rooms accessed via The Stairway. The player can buy pickups and items with coins.
The beggars have a very low chance to be replaced by another type of beggar.


== Conditions to Make Angel Rooms Appear ==
For the player to have a chance to get an Angel Room after killing a boss (or with a Joker card / Red Chest teleport), some conditions must be met:

A Devil Room door has spawned on any previous floor.
Teleporting to a Devil Room with a Joker card or a Red Chest doesn't count.
 Book of Virtues and the "You feel blessed!" fortune from Confessionals make the first deal to appear in a run to be an Angel Room.
No Deals with the Devil have been made throughout the run.
Taking Red Chest items, using Credit Card, using Coupon, or collecting an item from Krampus do not count.
Even though it technically doesn't cost any health, taking a Devil Deal with The Lost will still prevent Angel Rooms from appearing.
 Paying for Devil Room items from Boss Rooms after using Satanic Bible will still prevent Angel Rooms from spawning.
 Book of Virtues and Act of Contrition allow for Angel Rooms to spawn even if a Devil Deal was taken previously, as well as allowing to take Devil Deals without being locked out of Angel Rooms.
 The "You feel blessed!" fortune from Confessionals allow for Angel Rooms to spawn even if a Devil Deal was taken previously, but only for the current floor.


=== Sacrifice Room Exception ===
On the 3rd and 5th sacrifice in a Sacrifice Room, there is a 66% chance that the player will receive the "You feel blessed!" effect. This will increase the chances of the Angel Room spawning even if the previous conditions have not been met.
On the 6th sacrifice in a Sacrifice Room, there is a 33% chance that the player will be teleported to the Angel Room if they haven't already visited or opened the Devil Room for that floor. This will occur even if the previous conditions have not been met.


== Angel Room Generation Chance ==
The selection between Angel Room and Devil Room is made upon opening the door after defeating the floor's boss (or upon teleporting to the room using a Joker card or a Red Chest).
The game makes a series of coin flips to determine if an Angel Room will appear or not. If one of these coin flips succeeds, an Angel Room is generated (except for the Devil beggar coin flip). If all the coin flips fail or no coin flips are done, a Devil Room is generated. Satisfying certain conditions gives additional coin flips with varying probabilities:

** These conditions share the same "coin flip chance" in Rebirth.


=== Examples ===
If Isaac meets the prerequisites and has Key Piece 1 with him, the game will make two coin flips to determine if he gets an Angel Room or not. The first coin flip has a 50% success chance and the second one has a 25% success chance. Isaac will only get a Devil Room if both coin flips fail, and he will get an Angel Room if one of the coin flips succeeds. The chance of failure is 0.5 * 0.75 = 0.375, which means the chance of success is 1 - 0.375 = 0.625. Thus, Isaac has a 62.5% chance to get an Angel Room—take note that the result is not simply the sum of the coin flip probabilities 50% + 25% for 75%.
If Isaac meets the prerequisites, has Key Piece 1, and a Beggar paid on the current floor, the chance to fail all coin flips (and get a Devil Room) become 0.5 * 0.75 * 0.75 = 0.28125, which means that the chance of success is 1 - 0.28125 = 0.71875. Thus, Isaac has a 71.875% chance to get an Angel Room.


== Notes ==
The highest Angel Room chance is 95.25% in Rebirth and 98.34% in Afterbirth (with the Sacrifice Room blessings).
If an Angel Room spawns after the player defeats Mom's Heart or It Lives!, instead of items or pickups, a beam of light will appear. Touching this beam of light will take the player to the Cathedral. The Angel can still be awoken by destroying the statue in this room. The beam of light will disappear for the duration of the fight.
 Angel Rooms that spawn after Isaac defeats It Lives! will be normal Angel Rooms with items or pickups.
 The rock behind the Angel statue can rarely be a Tinted Rock.
 Two angel statues can appear in the same room, allowing Isaac to fight both Uriel and Gabriel. It is possible to get both Key Pieces if Isaac awakes and fights each of them one by one; however, fighting both at once will only spawn one Key Piece corresponding to the last defeated angel.
 Both angels can be fought at once, and will drop their corresponding Key Pieces as they die.
Contrary to popular belief, the Bible Tract doesn't allow Angel Rooms to appear after paying for a Devil Deal.

room_guides.Boss Rush:
The Boss Rush is an optional room that becomes available by beating Mom in Depths, Necropolis, or Dank Depths within 20 minutes, or  beating her in Mausoleum or Gehenna within 25 minutes.
In the center of a large room, there will be 4 ( 2 or 4 /  2, 4 or 8) random items to choose from, which are picked from the Treasure Room item pool. Take out Carrion Queen quickly, as its Red Poops will remain for the rest of the boss rush. They can be advantageous though, as other bosses can also take damage from these poops. In particular, bouncing bosses like The Hollow and The Husk can quickly kill themselves on contact.

The Bloat + Mask of Infamy is one of the hardest waves, but The Bloat can be baited into destroying both the heart and the mask itself of the Mask of Infamy with its Brimstone lasers.
Any teleport effect (such as cards, activated items, Telepills, etc) can be used to leave the Boss Rush. This can be used to gain one item without having to fight any bosses.
 After unlocking A Strange Door, Marked Skulls will always appear on Depths II and will always drop 0 - The Fool, providing a guaranteed way to escape Boss Rush.

room_guides.Challenge Room:
A Challenge Room is a special room that allows Isaac to fight enemies for extra rewards. They will only spawn on a floor if, upon entering the floor, Isaac's total health is greater than or equal to his number of heart containers. There are two kinds of challenge rooms: Normal Challenge Rooms, which appear on the first floor of a chapter or on Curse of the Labyrinth floors, and Boss Challenge Rooms, which appear on the second floor of a chapter. Challenge rooms do not appear in chapter 6.


== Normal Challenge Room ==

Normal Challenge Rooms can only be entered via their doors if Isaac's total health (Red, Black, and Soul Hearts) is greater than or equal to his number of heart containers. Picking up its contents will cause three waves of enemies to spawn. While in chapter 4 (Womb/Utero/Scarred Womb), 3 waves of bosses will be spawned, typically from Chapters 1 or 2. Each wave cleared will charge Isaac's active item by 1.


=== Waves ===
The enemies that spawn depend on the current chapter, and each chapter has two different possible sets of enemies:

== Boss Challenge Room ==

Boss Challenge Rooms will only spawn if Isaac has full health upon entering the second floor of a chapter, and can also only be entered via their doors if he has one or fewer hearts of health. Picking up its contents will cause two waves of bosses to spawn. Starting on Chapter 4, they use the same waves of bosses as Normal Challenge Rooms. Each wave cleared will charge Isaac's active item by 1. The Boss Challenge Room door only counts Red Hearts in determining whether Isaac is allowed to enter. Soul Hearts are ignored. Boss Challenge Rooms require one or fewer hearts total to enter, counting Soul Hearts. Boss Challenge Rooms will always contain an item from the Boss item pool.

room_guides.Challenges: '''Challenges''' are unique runs in the game. Isaac typically starts each challenge with one or more specific items which makes normal play more difficult. With few exceptions, {{R|Treasure Room}}s are not available during challenges. Challenges are all set in {{mode|normal}} normal mode except for [[I RULE!]]. Each challenge unlocks new content for the game, such as [[rune]]s, when completed. Players, with the advent of modding, can create their own [[Custom Challenges]] too. == General Strategy == Most challenges are designed to increase the difficulty of the game in a unique fashion. This doesn't mean all challenges are especially difficult. Challenges like [[Computer Savvy]] can be quite easy to beat, other challenges compensate for this by being especially punishing; [[Solar System]] being a good example of this. Each challenge has certain strategies that can be employed to make the run easier. However, there are a few strategies that can be applied to most challenges. * Challenges can be played in [[co-op]], allowing a second player to contribute to the run without being hindered in the same way Isaac is. This is especially useful in any challenge where Isaac is [[Blindfolded]], as the second player will be allowed to fire tears normally. ** {{dlc|r}} If other players join the game in the first room for true co-op, they will not get to select a character and will be forced to play as the character the challenge has you play as, ex. for [[Blue Bomber]], all players will be forced to play as {{c|???}} no matter what. (This excludes untrue co-op because of co-op babies.) * Due to the lack of {{R|Treasure Room}}s, {{R|Devil Room}}s become much more valuable. Some challenges can be made much easier by making just one deal, however many challenges reduce Isaac's health to the extent that Devil Deals become too risky. ** Some rooms (including {{R|Crawl Space}}s) may have Treasure Room items by default. Since these items are random, results can vary from run to run. *** {{dlc+|r}} Makes {{i|We Need To Go Deeper!}} useful, since it can open {{R|Crawl Space}}s each floor.{{dlc-}} ** Because locked Treasure Rooms don't spawn, keys can be used far more liberally. Also, [[trinket]]s and [[item]]s that generate more coins, along with upgraded {{R|Shop}}s, can help Isaac acquire a greater range of powerful items. * {{i|The Bible}} instantly kills {{E|Mom}} and {{E|Mom's Heart}} / {{E|It Lives!}}. All challenges require defeating Mom, and most require defeating Mom's Heart or It Lives!, making this an extremely powerful item, especially in challenges where Mom or Mom's Heart / It Lives! is the final boss. ** {{i|Pandora's Box}} will spawn {{I|The Bible}} if used in {{S|Womb}}/{{S|Utero}}/{{S|Scarred Womb}} II, making it a reliable way to acquire The Bible. ** {{p|XV - The Devil?}} can also do {{i|The Bible}}'s job. * {{R|Curse Room}}s can spawn items, making them valuable. * {{dlc|na}} In some challenges, {{R|Dice Room}}s and the {{i|D4}} are very useful, allowing that challenge's starting items to be rerolled, thus removing most of the difficulty. NOTE: This changes depending on the challenge. Most challenge pages contain details on the results of rerolling. ** {{t|Butter!}} can also remove starter items. * [[Blindfolded]] challenges are arguably the most difficult challenges due to Isaac's inability to fire tears. There are several methods to work around this. ** Familiars can provide an alternative method of dealing damage. Powerful familiars like {{i|Lil Brimstone}}, {{i|Succubus}}, {{i|Incubus}}, and {{i|Twisted Pair}} are therefore highly useful items. ** {{i|The Boomerang}}, {{i|The Candle}}, and {{i|Red Candle}} are also useful for blindfolded challenges, as they recharge based on a timer, rather than an amount of cleared rooms. ** {{e|Golden Bomb}} also provides a powerful damage output method for a floor. ** {{i|Clicker|dlc=nr}} can allow Isaac to change into {{C|Lilith}}, whose {{i|Incubus}} overrides the blindfolded effect by default. ** Some active items like {{i|Tammy's Head}} can be really helpful, providing an alternative method of dealing damage. ** {{dlc+|r}} {{i|Maw Of The Void}}, {{i|Revelation}}, and {{i|Montezuma's Revenge}} can be charged and fired even while Blindfolded, giving you very powerful attacks when you're not supposed to be able to shoot.{{dlc-}} ** Most useful items while blindfolded gain no benefit from the Tears, Range, or Shot Speed stats. As a result, items like {{i|False PHD}} can be used to make gains in other stats at effectively no cost. * {{i|Chaos}} is a powerful item in challenges, as it can allow powerful items to be found more commonly, such as in the Shop or after defeating bosses. * Defeating a boss beyond the specified end of the challenge (e.g. defeating {{E|Mom's Heart}} when the goal is to defeat {{E|Mom}}) will still spawn the trophy. ** {{dlc|anr}} In some longer challenges (e.g. [[XXXXXXXXL]]), using a {{R|Sacrifice Room}} until it teleports Isaac to the {{S|Dark Room}} is a viable strategy. Once in the Dark Room, the trophy can be spawned by defeating {{E|The Lamb}}. *** {{dlc+|a+nr}} In a similar vein, all runs can be completed by killing {{e|Delirium}}, meaning that the player can beat a challenge through an alternative method such as defeating {{E|Hush}} then traveling to {{S|The Void}}; however, this is generally extremely difficult given the restrictions challenges place on the player.{{dlc-}} == Notes == * Apart from the achievement related to beating the challenge, all achievements are locked. Also, no {{M|Donation Machine}}s will appear in any challenge. * {{C|Isaac}} does not start any challenge with {{i|The D6}}. * {{dlc+|r}} Items with tag [[Item Tags nochallenge|nochallenge]] are excluded during challenges. ** {{i|Lazarus' Rags}}, {{i|Judas' Shadow}}, {{i|Ankh}}, and {{i|Clicker}} are excluded, preventing Isaac from changing to other characters. *** {{dlc|nr+}} {{t|Broken Ankh}} is still available. *** {{dlc|r+}} {{t|Broken Ankh}}, {{t|Missing Poster}} and {{t|Mysterious Paper}} are also excluded. ** {{i|R Key}} is also excluded. ** Excluded items are considered as if they have not been unlocked, making it impossible to get these items by {{i|Spindown Dice}}, {{i|Bag of Crafting}}, or {{i|Death Certificate}}. ** It is, however, possible for [[Aprils Fool]]'s effect on active items to cause {{I|Clicker}} to activate.{{dlc-}} == Challenges List == {{challenge table}} {{nav|challenge|fr=Défis|ru=Испытания}} [[Category:Challenges| ]]
room_guides.Closet:
A closet is a rare, small, dead-end room added in The Binding of Isaac: Afterbirth. Closets often contain a unique arrangement of objects, pickups, items, or enemies, but are otherwise identical in appearance to normal rooms. Each chapter has several closet layouts, some differing between stages themselves. Some closets are considerably more rare than others, but also often contain more powerful loot or enemies.

room_guides.Crawl Space:
Crawl Spaces are small secret rooms that can be entered by touching trapdoors with ladders in them. They can be found by:

Using We Need To Go Deeper!  randomly (8% chance)/ on certain patterned tiles (100% chance once per floor)
Using Ehwaz  randomly (10% chance)/ on certain patterned tiles (100% chance once per floor)
Bombing a Clean Bedroom rug (100% chance)
Destroying a rock (see below)
 Using Chaos Card on Great Gideon (100% chance)
 Using XXI - The World? (100% chance)
These rooms are viewed from the side, rather than from above like the rest of the game, and Isaac will experience gravity pulling him to the floor while he is not walking on top of one of the ladders. Under the effects of flight, this gravity has no effects. However, Isaac cannot fly over the walls or floor. Items spawned inside are generated from the Treasure Room Item Pool.


== Mechanics ==
When entering a room pre-determined to contain a Crawl Space entrance, an RNG roll is made using the floor seed. This value will be shifted and divided, until its final result is in the grid range for the current room (ie: 128 tiles for 1x1 rooms, or 16x8). If said tile value is tied to a simple rock (not tinted, not a prop), then access to the Crawl Space will be granted upon destroying that rock. Only one room per floor has the right to spawn a Crawl Space, and not every floor is given one during the initial generation, even though every floor has also a Crawl Space and a Black Market ready in queue. The tile value can also be tied to props (empty tiles, doors, pots, void tiles, spikes, metal blocks, ...), but the Crawl Space won't spawn unless it's below a simple rock.

This makes the rocks contained in ??? have a significantly increased chance of spawning a crawl space.
 Crawl spaces may spawn under variants of rocks.


== Layouts ==
The following room maps were made using Basement Renovator for cleaner viewing.


== Notes ==
There is only one Crawl Space room per floor. Thus, if Isaac finds two trapdoors with ladders on the same floor, they will lead to the same Crawl Space. When Isaac exits the Crawl Space, he will come out from the entrance he came in from.  Creating a Crawl Space within a Crawl Space with XXI - The World? will just take Isaac back to the original one.
Entering a Crawl Space in the Boss Rush room and exiting it after the time limit has expired will transport Isaac back to the Mom Boss room.
There is no map in the Crawl Space, similar to the Black Market, the I AM ERROR room, the Devil Room, and the Angel Room.
This is because the Crawl Space does not technically occupy a fixed location on the floor relative to other rooms; Isaac is, in a sense, teleported to the Crawl Space when he touches the trapdoor. Possibly related to this, should Isaac enter a crawl space from a Devil Room, upon exiting he will emerge back in the regular map.
Be careful when using The Poop, as in certain situations, The Poop can block the exit and trap Isaac.
Crawl spaces can appear in Greed mode as well.
It is possible to enter Black Markets through a Crawl Space even when there is no path to it. By using two bombs, Isaac can clip out of bounds and then walk underneath the Crawl Space room.
 Leaving a Crawl Space from any side where no exit exists brings Isaac to I AM ERROR instead. It is now significantly more difficult to clip out of bounds, and can't be done with just two bombs.
 With Continuum, if Isaac shoots downward in a Crawl Space, his tears will continuously accelerate and may loop many times (over 20), regardless of his range.
 Rocks with Crawl Spaces under them will flash while holding the Shiny Rock.
 The trinket Stud Finder adds an additional 1 in 200 chance for a Crawl Space to appear when a rock is destroyed.
With Mom's Box or a Golden Trinket it becomes 1 in 100.
 The Crawl Space that appears by using a Chaos Card on Great Gideon always has the same design even if another Crawl Space was encountered.
 One Crawl Space layout contains two items, one of which is entirely enclosed by walls. The following are ways to obtain the seemingly off-limits item:
Teleport to it with Stitches;
Grab it with Mr. ME!;
Jump through the wall with How to Jump;
Using Void with Birthright when playing as Apollyon has a 10% chance to create a copy of the item after being absorbed by Void;
Absorb it with Moving Box, then place it in another room;
Clipping through the wall with Pluto;
Cloning the item using Diplopia and grabbing the copy created underneath.
This applies as well for Crooked Penny.
 Crawl Spaces can be found during the Mother's Shadow sequence. She will follow Isaac into them, so care must still be taken to avoid her charge.
The sequence may contain key blocks, usually with a key nearby. If a key is in your inventory when entering the crawl space, it will get transferred to your key pool, rendering a nearby key block impossible to remove.
 Crawl spaces can still be found on floors during the Ascent to Home.

The layout of the Crawl Space is a direct visual reference to the treasure rooms in the Legend of Zelda for the NES.
Crawl Spaces are referred to within the game files as "Item Dungeons".

room_guides.Curse Room:
Curse Rooms feature teeth-like spikes on the door that hurt Isaac when entering and exiting the room.
Curse rooms can appear from Chapter 1 to 5. Taking damage from the spikes doesn't reduce the odds of getting a Devil or Angel room.


== Layouts ==

== Notes ==
Items that grant flight allow Isaac to avoid damage taken upon entering a Curse Room, but do not prevent damage taken upon leaving.
Any item that gives Isaac a shield or invulnerability will prevent damage taken when passing through a Curse Room Door, including Holy Mantle.
If a Secret Room is next to a Curse Room, it can be entered without taking any damage by bombing the wall between these rooms from the Secret Room.
The damage done by the Curse Room's door is applied when touching the door. This means that Isaac can be damaged by it without actually going through the door, and any effects that occur upon taking damage will occur in the current room and not the room that the door leads to.
During Cursed! (challenge #10), all doors except for special types turn into this type of door.
Damage taken from entering a Curse Room doesn't count for the purposes of score calculation.
 Holding Flat File will remove the spikes from Curse Room doors, allowing them to be entered without taking damage.

The Curse Room's icon is similar to the icon of Whore of Babylon.

room_guides.Devil Room:
Devil Rooms primarily allow Isaac to make Deals with the Devil, but they can also contain a variety of enemies, pickups, or even a boss battle against Krampus. A Devil Room has a chance to appear in a Boss Room after the boss occupying it has been defeated. If certain criteria are met, a Devil Room can be replaced by an Angel Room. In Greed Mode, Devil Rooms are guaranteed to appear upon completing the optional 11th /  12th (in Greedier Mode) wave of a floor.

=== Greed Mode ===


== Deals with the Devil ==
A Devil Room has a high chance of spawning items that will be put up for sale. Unlike Shops, where Isaac pays with money, to make Deals with the Devil Isaac has to trade Red Heart Containers as payment. All items normally cost either 1 or 2 Red Heart Containers, and their prices roughly correspond to their power.
When playing as Keeper, the character's coin heart containers are used to trade for Devil Deal items, with items costing the same number of coin heart containers as red heart containers with a different character.

 Instead of coin heart containers, Devil Deal items must be bought using coins. One-heart and two-heart deals cost 15 and 30 cents, respectively. Paying cents for Devil Deals will still remove the Angel room appearance chance in the same way when other characters pay with heart containers.
The same cost for deals are applied with any character who collected A Pound of Flesh.
See the Devil Room item pool for a comprehensive list of items offered and their health price.  Additionally, Devil Deal items with the devilsacrifice item tag will have a sacrifice spike cost instead of a Red Heart Container cost. There is a 50% chance to award the item on the first play and 100% chance on the second. Picking up an item from the pedestal spawned this way counts as taking a regular deal and will prevent Angel Rooms from spawning naturally.


=== Notes ===
If Isaac does not have Red Heart Containers upon entering a Devil Room, all items will cost 3 Soul Hearts.
 If Isaac is presented with 2+ items to buy, but only has enough Red Hearts to buy one, the price of the other(s) will change to 3 Soul Hearts upon spending your Red Hearts.
 Additionally, if Isaac only has one Red Heart, deals that normally cost 2 Hearts will change to one Red Heart and two Soul Hearts.
If Isaac does not have enough Soul Hearts for this type, he will still be able to take the Deal. However, if Isaac has no health at all (e. g. he is defying death with Berserk!), he will not be able to take the Deals.
 If Isaac has less than 3 Soul Hearts, but at least one Bone Heart, he can take a three-Soul-Heart Deal and stay alive because of the bone hearts.
 Bone hearts are considered Heart Containers. Having at least one bone heart will change the price of a Deal to at least one red heart.
Two-heart deals can be taken even if Isaac does not have enough Red Hearts to afford them, as long as he has one Red Heart to spend.
Spending all of his Heart Containers will not kill Isaac as long as he has Soul Hearts, Black Hearts, or Bone Hearts remaining.
If taking a Deal leaves Isaac with no health remaining, he can still survive if he picks up a Soul Heart, Black Heart, or Bone Heart while holding the item in the air. Also, if he has an active item that grants Soul/Black Hearts, he can take a Deal and then use the active item, leaving him alive with whatever the item gave him. The same is true for consumables that give hearts (e. g. Dagaz).
 If Isaac takes a Deal for an item that grants an Eternal Heart through the use of Chaos, it will not keep him alive.
 The temporary heart container granted by XI - Strength cannot be used to purchase a devil deal. However, if Isaac has no other heart containers to spend, then it can be used this way. This also works if the devil deal costs 2 hearts, but Isaac only has 0 or 1 before activating the Strength card.
 Temporary heart containers can be used for devil deals with no restrictions.
 Some items may cost Soul Hearts even if Isaac still has Red Hearts.
An item's price may change from Red Hearts to Soul Hearts if Isaac visits the Devil Room before obtaining enough Soul Hearts and returning to the Devil Room.


=== Angel Rooms ===
Refusing to make Deals with the Devil will give Isaac the chance of an Angel Room replacing the Devil Room on subsequent floors. If any Deal with the Devil is taken, Angel Rooms will not spawn for the remainder of the run.
 Trading Heart Containers for items in a Black Market counts as taking a Deal with the Devil for Angel Room generation purposes.
Only the act of paying health (Red Hearts or Soul Hearts) for an item in a Devil Room counts as a Deal with the Devil. Taking Black Hearts, opening Red Chests, and taking items that weren't paid for (such as those obtained from Red Chests, Krampus, Beggars, Pandora's Box, or made free by using Credit Card) do not count as Deals taken, allowing Isaac to still see Angel Rooms.
 If the first offered Devil Room is not entered at all, the next offer is guaranteed to be an Angel Room. If the player uses the Joker it will take you to the Angel Room without removing the guarantee.


== Conditions to Make Devil Rooms Appear ==
A Devil Room can only open on floors between the second floor of Chapter 1 and Chapter 4.
There is only a 1% base chance for the Devil Room door to open. This chance can be modified in various ways:

For example, if Isaac has avoided taking Red Heart damage and has blown up a Shopkeeper, he will have a (1+35+99+10)% = 145% base Deal with the Devil chance which will be displayed 100%, which will then go down to 36.25% once he sees the Devil Room.


== Notes ==
If the player enters a Devil Room without the entrance door appearing (by teleporting in), the chance to receive a Devil Room will not be reduced. Because of this, if a Devil Room is seen this way and the player does not want to enter it again, intentionally taking red heart damage will reduce the chance of seeing it after the boss fight, which can prevent the penalty from seeing the Devil Room door from applying to the next floor.
The chance that the Devil Room or Angel Room door will remain open after re-entering the Boss Room is based on the current Deal with the Devil chance, which gains the x0.25 multiplier from seeing the Devil Room door less than two floors ago. Due to its high chance of disappearing, it is recommended to go directly into the Devil Room when offered,  unless it's the first time one is seen and the player wants to get a guaranteed Angel deal.
Once a Devil Room door closes for the floor, it cannot be re-opened without picking up Goat Head or Eucharist.
On XL floors, the Devil Room door can only appear after completing the second Boss Room.
On XL floors, not seeing a Devil Room will count as not seeing a Devil Room for two floors, and seeing it will count as not seeing a Devil Room for one floor.
Taking Soul Heart, Black Heart, Eternal Heart, Bone Heart, or Rotten Heart damage does not decrease the chance to open a Devil Room; only Red Hearts count.
Taking red heart damage from a Devil Beggar, Blood Donation Machine, IV Bag, Blood Rights, Razor Blade, Shard of Glass or Sharp Plug does not decrease the chance to open a Devil Room.
 Sacrifice Rooms also count as self-damage and do not lower the Devil Room chance.
 The Bad Trip pill effect or damage from Curse Room doors still counts as Red Heart damage.
 Losing a Bone Heart container as The Forgotten counts as Red Heart damage.
Tainted Magdalene's leaking Red Hearts being damaged does not count as Red Heart damage, regardless of the damage source.
There are additional ways to enter a Devil Room on any floor:
Red Chests have a chance of teleporting Isaac into the Devil Room upon being opened.
Using Joker will teleport Isaac into the room.
 Using Teleport 2.0 after all other rooms on the floor (excluding the I AM ERROR room) have been visited.
Teleport!, Undefined, and Telepills cannot transport Isaac to the Devil Room.
 If a deal would deal lethal damage to The Soul, quickly switching to The Forgotten will keep him alive. This can even be done to take 3-heart deals for one soul heart.
If The Soul has no Hearts, switching to The Soul is disabled until another Soul or Black Heart is acquired.
 The same can be done "in reverse" - take a deal as The Forgotten and quickly switch to The Soul. However, this will usually cause a softlock unless Birthright is obtained since switching to The Forgotten will be disabled while he has no Hearts, and The Soul is chained to The Forgotten and thus is incapable of traversing rooms.
 The Lost can take all Deals with the Devil for free.
 The Lost, Tainted Lost, and Tainted Jacob in ghost form are allowed to take one of the offered Deals for free; the others will vanish afterward.
The same applies to any character turned into ghost form via Soul of the Lost or by touching a White Fire Place.
 ??? pays for Devil Deals with Soul Hearts for prices equal to their Red heart equivalent; ie, one or two Soul Hearts depending on the item, rather than the normal three. No other character has this effect, including Tainted ???.
 The rock behind the Devil can rarely be a Tinted Rock.
 An Angel statue can rarely substitute the Satan statue and can be awoken with an explosion as usual.
Angels spawned in this way do not drop Key Pieces, however.
The highest possible Devil Room chance without Goat Head is 204% in Afterbirth, or 326.9% in Repentance.
 It is possible to have a guaranteed Deal Chance without Goat Head or Eucharist if enough Satanic Bible wisps are produced and all chance-increasing effects take place. However, this is extremely difficult to achieve since only up to 8 Satanic Bible wisps can exist simultaneously (certain items such as Jar of Wisps ignore this).
Teleporting into a deal without beating the floor boss can generate a different deal than the one you'd receive after beating it. This can be observed by having a Red Chest teleport or using a Joker while holding on to a Glowing Hourglass, using it to undo the teleport and then accessing the deal after defeating the floor boss, even if the deal door does not open by itself.
This can be observed even in the starting floor of the game. It however no longer happens after Womb 2.
Once a deal has been generated in any manner, it can not be changed or influenced.
For example collecting Eucharist after a Devil Deal door had opened, will not result into changing the current floor deal to an Angel Deal even if the Devil Deal was not visited.
It is possible to "undo" a deal door opening after beating the floor boss with Glowing Hourglass (provided the natural chance for the deal was not 100%) by entering the deal door and using the hourglass inside the room. If that happens, the game considers the current deal as not having opened at all, and will not apply a deal chance penalty for the next floor. This can be useful if the deal did not offer anything the player wanted.
This can be repeated as many times as necessary until the door closes by itself, and as long as Isaac directly visits the deal and does not leave it himself but only by using the hourglass.

room_guides.Dice Room:
Dice Rooms  are special rooms that can randomize many elements of the run. Dice Rooms require two Keys to be opened, unlike most other special rooms. For a Dice Room to spawn,  two things must happen;

First, the game must decide that a Sacrifice Room will spawn that floor. This normally has a 1/7 (~14%) chance of happening each floor, but increases to 5/14 (~36%) if Isaac’s total health (filled red and soul hearts) is equal to or greater than his total Red Heart  Containers (including Bone Hearts).
Once the game determines a Sacrifice Room will spawn, a Dice Room has a 1/50 (2%) chance to replace it. This chance increases to 27/125 (~22%) if Isaac has two or more keys.


== Effects ==

In addition to whatever else the room holds, there will always be a symbol of one of the sides of a six-sided die in the 5x5 center of the room. The amount of pips shown will be between one to six, chosen randomly. When Isaac crosses the die, a certain effect will occur that randomizes a certain aspect of the run, dependent on how many pips were on the die face shown. Any given Dice Room can only give this effect once.
The die numbers and effects are:

⚀ 1 pip -  Rerolls Isaac's currently held collectibles into items from the Treasure Room item pool, like the D4 would. Activated collectibles can be changed into passive ones, but passive collectibles cannot turn into activated ones.
 Rerolls each of Isaac's passive items into a random item from the pool of the room where it was acquired.
 Rerolls both Isaac's active and passive items.
 Only rerolls the items of the character that stepped onto the dice in co-op.
Meaning that Tainted Forgotten has to be thrown on the button in order to take effect.
⚁ 2 pips - Rerolls all pickups in the room, like the D20 would.
⚂ 3 pips - Rerolls all pickups and trinkets on the entire floor. This includes Shop pickups. Does not reroll pickups or trinkets in the Devil Room, Angel Room, Black Market, or Crawl Space.
Pickups rerolled in shops by this effect have a chance to turn into items. If these are active items, they will have no charges when picked up.
⚃ 4 pips - Rerolls any item pedestals on the floor, like The D6 would. Does not reroll item pedestals in the Devil Room, Angel Room, Library, Black Market, or Crawl Space.
⚄ 5 pips - Rerolls and restarts the current floor, which is the same effect as Forget Me Now.
⚅ 6 pips - Combines the effects of the 1-, 3-, and 4-pip rooms. (Rerolls all held items (including active), pickups, trinkets, and pedestal items like the D100.)
 Rerolls all held items for all characters in co-op.

== Notes ==
Dad's Key, Get out of Jail Free Card, Mr. ME!, and Sharp Key open Dice Rooms in one use.
Due to how Dice Room generation works, a floor cannot have both a Dice Room and Sacrifice Room; they are mutually exclusive.
If a floor has two special rooms that require two keys to enter, the one closer to the start room will be a Vault, and the one further away from it will be a Dice Room.
It is possible to re-roll a floor into another that has a 5-pip Dice Room. Getting a 5-pip dice room in Womb / Utero II can allow the player to defeat Mom's Heart (or It Lives!) multiple times in one run. This can be used to quickly gain progress tied to the number of Mom's Heart kills.
It is possible to unlock Samson by finishing the first floor and using a 5-pip Dice Room.
A 5-pip dice room on an XL floor sends Isaac to the first floor of the chapter.
When shop pickups are re-rolled via a 3- or 6-pip room, the original prices will remain in place.
3- or 6-pip Dice Rooms can reroll chests in Challenge Rooms or Boss Challenge Rooms into collectibles. And since those rooms detect whether a chest is open or an item picked up, there won't be any monsters.
3-pip room can re-roll shop pickups into items.
Using items such as The D6 in the room without buying the item can cause the item to revert to a pickup.
There is a small chance that 1- and 6-pip rooms will not reroll every item Isaac has in his possession.
 Dice Rooms don't re-roll starter challenge items or remove blindfold on challenges.
 Dice Rooms have a small marker indicating the effect that will be activated when the room is used. This was inspired by this Steam Workshop mod by Wofsauge.
 If Jacob and Esau activate a 6-pip room, the items held by both characters will be rerolled, but only the items of the character that step on a 1-pip room will be rerolled.
 Any rooms generated by Red Key that contain an item pedestal will not be affected by a 4-pip room.
 In the Mirrored World, the second Dice Room may be different.
 If Tainted Lazarus activates a 1-pip room, only the state that activated the room will have the items rerolled, leaving the other form's items untouched.

room_guides.I AM ERROR:
The I AM ERROR room is a rare room that isn't connected to any other room on the floor and is reached through glitches or as a failsafe for an impossible event (like using Blank Card on ? Card, which loops on itself infinitely without a failsafe).
I AM ERROR rooms are chaotic and often contain multiple items, pickups, beggars, and/or powerful enemies. There are no doors to leave, but always an exit to the next level ( with few exceptions) and at least one unique shopkeeper (pictured above) with a text bubble that reads "I AM ERROR".
The trapdoor will always be open, even if there are enemies in the room.


== Accessing the I AM ERROR room ==
The only items/effects that can bring Isaac to the I AM ERROR room are Telepills, Undefined, Teleport 2.0, Red Key and Blank Card + ? Card. (This consumes Blank Card and ? Card)
Undefined is the simplest method, as it has a decent chance to teleport the player there.
 Using Red Key on the 13x13 boundaries of the map will create a 1-way door to the I AM ERROR room, and displays no icon on the map upon opening.
No red door outlines will appear on the normal floor's boundary walls, meaning the I AM ERROR room can only be entered from another Red Room. At least 2 uses of Cracked Key are needed to enter if you don't have access to Red Key.
Doesn't work on the Chest, Dark Room, The Void, Home, Corpse II, or the Dad's Note floor.
 Using Teleport 2.0 when all rooms on the floor have been explored (including the Secret Room(s), Super Secret Room(s), and the Devil Room or Angel Room) sends you to the I AM ERROR room.
 The I AM ERROR room can be reached by leaving a Crawl Space through an unintended direction. This will always bring you to an error room, even when all other methods stop working.
Blank Card + XXI - The World?, Clear Rune + Ehwaz, We Need To Go Deeper!, and Mom's Shovel offer consistent methods of creating crawl spaces.
Use 4 size downs, 2 speed, and crash into the floor below the entrance ladder or 3 size downs and the left and right walls using flight.
One makes you smaller is the easiest way to acquire multiple size downs, and although you can exit the crawl space using listed minimums, it sometimes requires a lot of patience. Pluto / Inner Child are equal to 4 uses of the pill.
It is also possible to exit through an unintended direction using A Pony / White Pony and 1 size down, albeit rarely. Significantly more common with 2 or more size downs. The speed stat does not matter since the charge-speed is a flat velocity.
You can use Spin to Win, 2 speed & flight just by themselves to exit, bouncing off the far left and right walls and timing turning around after each bounce to build up speed and eventually exit.
Tainted Forgotten can be thrown outside the Crawl Space provided Tainted Soul builds up enough velocity, resulting in accessing the I AM ERROR room.
The Forgotten can place his body at the bottom of the entrance ladder, swap to the Soul form, then stretch vertically towards the entrance. Slingshotting yourself downward using the chain can provide some extra speed in order to clip.
 A trapdoor created in the Lil Portal bedroom with We Need To Go Deeper! or Ehwaz will always lead to the I AM ERROR room.


== I AM ERROR room destination ==
Entering the I AM ERROR room from Womb II, Utero II, Scarred Womb II or ??? will randomly result in a trapdoor or a beam of light. Isaac may have to end his run early in the Cathedral/Sheol if the wrong story item was collected.
 The second part of each Alt floor shall send Isaac back to the main route. (for example, Downpour II's trapdoor goes to Caves II.)
 The only way to access the I AM ERROR room on Chest, Dark Room, The Void, Home, Corpse II, or the Dad's Note floor is through glitching out of bounds inside of a Crawl Space. Methods such as Teleport 2.0 will instead create an I am Error Shopkeeper.
Chest and Dark Room's I AM ERROR room contain a portal to The Void.
If The Void is not unlocked, it will instead contain a trapdoor that brings Isaac back to the floor.
This is the same case if Isaac enters the I AM ERROR room when on Mausoleum II via inserting The Polaroid or The Negative into the Strange Door on Depths II. This will simply take Isaac to the starting room instead of taking him to Mausoleum II as to continue to Ascent route.
Corpse II, Home, The Void, and the Dad's Note floor all have I AM ERROR room which contains a trapdoor that puts Isaac back onto the floor.
 In the rare event of accessing I AM ERROR on Corpse XL and encountering a trapdoor in that error room, Isaac is taken to a new floor which attempts to load then the game crashes.
 Entering the I AM ERROR room in Corpse XL will create a trapodoor or a beam of light that sends Isaac to Cathedral or Sheol, similarly to Womb II, Utero II, Scarred Womb II or ???.
This can be viewed by enabling the LABY RNTH seed and getting into the Corpse XL Error room.
 Entering the exit of an I AM ERROR room in the Chest or Dark Room will restart the floor.
 The I AM ERROR room cannot be reached in Chest, Dark Room, or the final floor of the daily challenge.
 During the Ascent, the I AM ERROR room will contain a beam of light instead.


== Layouts ==

== Notes ==
Once Isaac arrives at the I AM ERROR room, the only ways out are the trapdoor to the next level or another teleport. As the I AM ERROR room is randomly reached, this could force Isaac to skip Treasure Room and/or Boss Room items if they hadn't been picked up before, and if he cannot teleport again.
Items in the I AM ERROR room will be from random item pools.
 Once Corrupted Data is achieved (beating Delirium as Tainted Eden), items that spawn in this room have a 1/16 chance to be randomized as if affected by TMTRAINER.
If a Crawl Space is spawned in the I AM ERROR room, Isaac will return to the room he was in before being teleported to the I AM ERROR room upon exiting the Crawl Space.
Using the trapdoor in the I AM ERROR room can allow Isaac to reach levels not yet unlocked, like Sheol or Cathedral.
 Using the trapdoor in Chest or the Dark Room will restart the level, similar to the effect of the Forget Me Now, and as of patch 1.05, the floor will generate a different layout upon restarting. The door to Mega Satan will be locked if it was previously opened.
The chests present in the I AM ERROR room while on Chest and Dark Room always contain items.
Using the Jera in most of these room configurations can allow Isaac to duplicate a very large amount of pickups, making Jera especially effective in this room.
If Isaac is teleported to a Devil Room or Angel Room from an I AM ERROR room (e. g. by using Joker), exiting the room will return him to the room he was in before entering the I AM ERROR room.
It is probably not a good idea to go to the I AM ERROR room on Depths/Necropolis/Dank Depths II before getting The Polaroid/The Negative, because then you can't go to the Chest or Dark Room, having to end the run in Sheol or Cathedral.
Reaching another I AM ERROR room in the above-mentioned levels would allow continuing the run beyond them, even lacking the prerequisite items.
Note that the 12th reward and onward in a Sacrifice Room has a 50% chance to send Isaac to Dark Room. This may be useful if an I AM ERROR room locked Isaac out of The Negative.
 This rule also applies to Isaac when trying to reach an alternate floor from a main floor (Downpour II from Basement II, etc.). The I AM ERROR room will always send him to a regular floor (Basement II to Caves I, etc.) and Isaac will not be able to pick up the necessary progression items needed to reach Corpse.
However, in Mausoleum/Gehenna II, if Isaac kills Mom's Heart first, then enters the I AM ERROR room, the trapdoor inside will lead him to Corpse.
 There is a rare Closet room in Depths and Necropolis containing an I AM ERROR shopkeeper. This is not an I AM ERROR room, and can be exited normally.
 There is a Super Secret Room that looks like an I AM ERROR room. This is not an I AM ERROR room, and can be exited normally.


== Trivia ==
The I AM ERROR room is a reference to an infamous quote in the NES game Zelda II: The Adventure of Link, where a citizen from Ruto introduces himself with the sentence "I AM ERROR".

The weight represents how likely it is for the game to spawn the item. Nearly every item in the game has a weight of 1. ** For example, if there are 200 items in a given item pool, and each item has a weight of 1, that means there is a 1 in 200 (0.5%) chance to get any particular item from that pool. ** However, if an item has a weight of 0.5, that means that item is 50% as likely to spawn compared to an item that has a weight of 1. In a pool of 200 items that has only 2 items with a weight of 0.5, that would result in the total weight being 199. ((198 * 1) + (2 * 0.5) = 199) This means items with a weight of 1 have a 1 in 199 (≈0.5%) chance to spawn, while an item with a weight of 0.5 has a 1 in 398 (≈0.25%) chance to spawn. * {{dlc|nr}} Only automatically decremented inside of the respective item pool. However, the amount of the decrementation varies depending on the specific item pool. * If an item happens to be in more than one item pool, the weight decrementation will also apply to other pools. * Touching an item will remove it from all item pools. * If a pedestal cycles between multiple items, such as from {{i|Glitched Crown}}, each item option will count as being seen. The seen items in the following item pools are decremented by 50% on sight: * [[Beggar (Item Pool)|Beggar]] * [[Bomb Bum (Item Pool)|Bomb Bum]] * [[Curse Room (Item Pool)|Curse Room]] and [[Curse Room (Greed Mode Item Pool)|Greed Mode Curse Room]] * [[Devil Beggar (Item Pool)|Devil Beggar]] * [[Key Master (Item Pool)|Key Master]] * {{dlc|r}} [[Battery Bum (Item Pool)|Battery Bum]] * {{dlc|nr}} [[Shop (Item Pool)|Shop]] and [[Shop (Greed Mode Item Pool)|Greed Mode Shop]] * {{dlc|r}} [[Mom's Chest (Item Pool)|Mom's Chest]] The seen items in the following item pools are decremented by 40% on sight: * [[Golden Chest (Item Pool)|Golden Chest]] and [[Golden Chest (Greed Mode Item Pool)|Greed Mode Golden Chest]] * [[Red Chest (Item Pool)|Red Chest]] * {{dlc|r}} [[Ultra Secret Room (Item Pool)|Ultra Secret Room]] * {{dlc|r}} [[Old Chest (Item Pool)|Old Chest]] The seen items in the following item pools are decremented by 10% on sight: * [[Library (Item Pool)|Library]] and [[Library (Greed Mode Item Pool)|Greed Mode Library]] * {{dlc|r}} [[Crane Game (Item Pool)|Crane Game]] All other item pools not listed above are fully decremented on sight, and thus, removed. === Examples === * All items in the Treasure Room pool are completely decremented on sight. Thus, seeing a {{i|Notched Axe}} in the Basement 1 Treasure Room will make it impossible to spawn another Notched Axe in the run. (In this case, players do '''not''' have to touch the Notched Axe in order to prevent the game from ever spawning another one.) * {{dlc|nr}} All items in the shop pool are decremented by 0.5 on sight. room_guides.Library:
A Library is a room that must be opened with a key. Items from the Library item pool can be found within, among other things, such as cards and/or runes or even enemies. Libraries have a 5% chance of appearing each floor. Certain Library layouts can only appear after unlocking certain store upgrades from donating to the Donation Machine.


== Layouts ==
The following room maps were made using Basement Renovator for cleaner viewing.


== Notes ==
 From the outside, the library is identical in appearance to the Shop. One of the ways they can be distinguished is if Isaac has a mapping item such as Spelunker Hat or The Compass. Generally, the library will be closer to the starting room than the Shop.
 The library now has its own unique door.
Once all items in the Library item pool have been picked up, items from the Treasure Room item pool will appear instead.
Libraries are particularly useful for acquiring the Bookworm transformation.
NO! now replaces all activated items inside the Library with passive items, which prevents all Library items other than Book of Virtues from appearing.


== Trivia ==
The music that plays in the Library is the same as the one played in ending 14.
room_guides.Mini-Boss Room:
The Mini-Boss Room is a Special Room in which Isaac battles against one of a number of mini-bosses, namely the Seven Deadly Sins, their Super variants, and Ultra Pride.  The Super Sins cannot be encountered in Basement or its variants; they only appear in Mini-Boss Rooms starting from Caves and beyond. If a Red Room created by Red Key (etc.) is a Mini-Boss Room, all Sins and their variants, as well as Krampus, can be found within, even in the Basement.
As opposed to most other Special Rooms, Isaac can't tell this type of room from the appearance of the door without items that reveal this information, like The Compass or Spelunker Hat, making the encounter a surprise. Once entered, all doors will be barred with two horizontal wood planks and metal, making it impossible to escape by blasting them open with bombs.
It has three properties that are shared with many special rooms:

Not every floor contains a Mini-Boss Room.
No floor may contain more than one.
It is always a dead end, except for a fight against Greed or Super Greed in a Secret Room.
Standard Mini-Boss Rooms can spawn on any floor up to Chapter 5. In Chapter 6, Mini-Boss Rooms do not appear except for Greed or Super Greed in the Secret Room. However, mini-bosses are frequently encountered as regular enemies.


== Notes ==
A door leading to a Mini-Boss Room cannot be bombed open.
Using Dad's Key, a Get out of Jail Free Card or Mr. ME! can open the door.
room_guides.Planetarium:
The Planetarium is an unlockable room type added in The Binding of Isaac: Repentance. Planetariums are similar to Treasure Rooms, in that they both require keys to enter, but always contain special astronomy-themed items that are only available through Planetariums. Their chance for appearing increases with each Treasure Room skipped. They are unlocked by acquiring three different astrology-related items in a single run.


== Generation Chance ==
Planetariums can only appear in chapters 1, 2, and 3 (Including their alternative floors).

Telescope Lens allows Planetariums to generate in Womb and Corpse.
However, Planetariums can appear in the additional Mausoleum II / Gehenna II level that is accessed through A Strange Door.
The base chance for a Planetarium to generate is 1%. This chance can be modified in various ways:

In other words, every Treasure Room skipped will add 20% to the generation chance. However, if additional Treasure Rooms are entered, such as those created by Forget Me Now or Red Key, then the 20% penalty for entering a Treasure Room will be taken without receiving the 20% bonus for descending a floor.

The combined percentage from descending floors and entering Treasure Rooms will never go below 0%.
Entering Treasure Rooms in the Mirrored World of Downpour II / Dross II will not affect the generation chance.


== Layouts ==
The following room maps were made using Basement Renovator for cleaner viewing.


== Notes ==
The Crystal Ball and Deck of Cards will not count towards the unlock if they are left behind after picking them up, they must be actively held.
If Isaac loses passive items (ie: using the D4) they will not count towards the unlock. In other words, Isaac must have 3 items simultaneously.
Planetarium items can be found before Planetariums have been unlocked in-game. To do so, use any method that ignores item pools (Chaos, Eden, etc.).
If attempting to find a Planetarium to obtain one of its items, very careful consideration should be taken before picking up Rosary, as this will add The Bible to the Planetarium's item pool. Given the pool's small size, you will have a high chance to find it instead of a normal Planetarium item.
A simple way to unlock Planetariums is to acquire a D20 in Greed Mode and re-roll the coins to keep buying store items (this requires a battery to recharge the D20). The item pool includes Magic 8 Ball and all Treasure Room items (which include most of the pertinent items); therefore, it can easily be unlocked.
Acquiring the astrology-related items from the Bag of Crafting will not guarantee the Planetarium achievement.
However, acquiring the regular Zodiac items via Bag of Crafting will grant the achievement.
If a Planetarium has been generated, XVII - The Stars will prioritize teleporting Isaac into it over the Treasure Room.
If a Planetarium appears on Downpour II, even if the door has been unlocked, the planetarium in the Mirrored World will be locked and will contain nothing.
Planetariums will not be available on challenges that prevent Treasure Rooms from spawning.
During Pica Run (challenge #41), a Planetarium will contain only a trinket.
If Isaac uses Glowing Hourglass to exit a Planetarium upon first entering one, the Planetarium does not count as entered, and Planetarium chance is preserved for later floors, allowing Isaac to effectively reroll his Planetarium until a desired item is found.
Doing a Victory Lap does not reset the entered Treasure Room count, making it very difficult to have a high chance for Planetarium generation.
Using R Key resets the entered Treasure Room count.
If the Planetarium layout selected was a closet-sized room, and there are no valid locations for it to spawn, then the Planetarium will not generate.
Leaving an XL floor will count as descending 2 floors.


== General Strategy ==
Overall, the Planetarium items are average to above-average. None of them are bad, but none of them are particularly gamebreaking either. So, given that skipping a treasure room doesn't guarantee a Planetarium showing up, it usually isn't worth skipping Treasure Rooms without a good reason to do so unless you're doing speedruns. In speedruns the global strategy is to skip everything to go to the last floor. So in that case, Terra and Mercurius are the best items and overall skipping Treasure rooms is always worth since we can have a build with only Devil or Angel deals.
Given the Ascent path takes Isaac back through previous floors, it is viable to skip item rooms on the way down to improve his chances of the Planetarium spawning and then getting the items from the rooms he skipped on the way back up. However, Planetariums can NOT generate during the Ascent, nor will skipped Planetariums "reappear".
Items such as Glowing Hourglass or Dream Catcher can be used to check the contents of a Treasure Room without negatively affecting the chances for a Planetarium to spawn.


== Statistics ==
Without Telescope Lens, Planetarium rooms can't be found in chapter 4 and after. Since the chance to find a Planetarium depends on the number of Treasure Rooms skipped, skipping earlier ones allows for a higher cumulative chance of encountering one.
The table below presents the chances if the first Treasure Rooms are skipped. For example, if the first two are passed on, there is an 84% chance to find a Planetarium between Basement I and Depths I.
